title: rules.version.published.v1
description: Written to the Rule Engine outbox in the transaction where a second person approves a PENDING_APPROVAL version (POST .../versions/{v}:approve, DESIGN section 3.3). The version is PUBLISHED and takes effect at effectiveFrom; caches are invalidated after commit. The outbox row id is the event id. Additive changes only within v1.

eventId.description: The event id, a ULID; equal to the outbox row id. Consumers de-duplicate by it.

occurredAt.description: When the state change committed, ISO 8601 UTC.

tenantId.description: The tenant, from the authenticated context; never from a request body.

correlationId.description: The caller's correlation id (X-Correlation-Id, or the one passed to the Java API). When the caller gave none, the event id: the event starts its own chain.

causationId.description: The id of the command or event that caused this one, or null when a caller's command caused it directly.

producer.description: rule-engine, a slash and the engine version that wrote the event.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the envelope layout; 1 for every .v1 type.

version.description: Version number of the rule set, not the lock version.

canonicalHash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical document, lower-case hex: the behaviour under four eyes (ADR-0026). effectiveFrom is not part of it.

effectiveFrom.description: The instant the version takes effect, ISO 8601 UTC: the requested date, or the approval instant when none was requested. Never null on this event.

approvedBy.description: Who approved it; always equal to actor, and never the requester or the author (four eyes).

acknowledgedWarnings.description: The { code, input } pairs the approver accepted on the record (PD-104, RLE-053): exactly the pairs that needed an acknowledgement at approval, empty when none did.

maskedByDefaultInputs.description: Inputs that declare no mask and were masked only by the tenant's decision-log.mask-default at approval, sorted; empty when none. They needed no acknowledgement, and would reach the decision log in plain text if the default were later turned off (PD-104).
